en: K4 was checked up to 82b4 [dvādaśāha] 12.1–2 [K1,81b8;
K4,81b9: *hariḥ śrīrāmāya namaḥ śrīgovindāya* (EM)].
Those intending to undergo initiation for the twelve-day sacrifice (*dvādaśāha*) assemble together.

One who is about to sacrifice with the Aptoryāma initiates himself with a thousand, ten thousand, and eight animals. There are twelve *upasads*. They proceed from the *upavasatha* day according to the established ritual procedure. He proceeds with the animal sacrifice to Agni and Soma. At the conclusion of the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings, having offered the night-oblations (*niśāhuti*) and carried around the *vasatīvarī* waters, they set aside the milks and observe the fast. In the morning, having taken the clarified butter portions and brought down King Soma, he begins the *prātaranuvāka* recitation. When it has been concluded—

At the morning recitation (prātaranuvāka), he says "apo śāñce" [K4: *apo śaity*]; having poured out water and offered the residue (saṃsrāva) into the Āhavanīya fire, and having performed the Atirātra sacrifice, he enters the Prājāpatya [K4: *prājāpatyan*].

He offers the *dadhigraha* for his husband; having caused [the sacrificer] to recite over the *nigrābhyā* waters, he takes the *udābhya* from the very [vessel] that was bound and offers it. Then, taking the *upāṃśusavana* stone, he measures out the King [Soma]. Having brought water and satisfied [himself], he recites the verses for the *prāṇagrahas* and the first *pṛśni* cups, and the verses for the *apānagrahas* and the subsequent *pṛśni* cups. Having taken a shoot (*aṃśu*) from that which has been pressed once, he offers it; in this manner, these two [offerings].

He takes [the draughts]; wherever he takes them, having performed the *upāṃśu* rite, he offers the *upāṃśu* oblation. Having pressed [the Soma], he takes [the draughts] starting from the *āgrayaṇa* in the established manner; having taken the *āgrayaṇa*, he takes the *ṣoḍaśin* with the verse, "Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra. He takes the cake with [the verse], "Mount... O slayer of Vṛtra..."

With the words "dā," he draws the three *pṛṣṭhya* cups, he draws the *ukthya*, he draws the *dhruva*, and he purifies the *śukra*. At that very point, he issues the command: "O *Āgnīdh*, spread the fires; turn [the ladle]."

"Bring the grass for the sacrificial enclosure outside; prepare the *puroḍāśa* cakes; O Pratiprasthātṛ, bring the animal victim. Regarding this, they say: the Pratiprasthātṛ brings the animal victim after having presented the King (Soma); having performed the sacrifice according to the respective deities, having taken the draught for the Aśvins, having moved about with the *grahāvakāśas*, and having gone out, he binds the eight cords... [the pressing-wood] by means of the impulsion (*prasava*), separately for each of its own forms.

(22) Whether [the animal sacrifice] is performed with various animals, or with one, or with both—then, having taken up sixteen *barhis* blades with the formula "For food, thee! (*iṣe tvā*) and having offered the introductory oblations (*upākaraṇīya*), he dedicates the animals: a goat for Agni as the *savanīya* animal, one for Indra-Agni as the *ukthya* animal, one for Indra for the *ṣoḍaśin*, and one for Sarasvatī which is to come. For the night, [he takes] six *pṛṣṭhya* [stotras]... at the end... having proceeded with the omenta...

(24) Having performed the ritual with the omenta (*vapā*), they proceed: for the *pṛṣṭhya* [stomas], the *anāheya*, the *aindra*, the *saurya*, and the *prājāpatya* [offerings]; for the *aptoryāma*, the animals [are offered]. Having proceeded with their omenta in the established manner, they move forward. The *aptoryāma-atirātra* sacrifice is performed; it is successfully completed. <12.2> [K4,82a1; M403-4]

The Pṛṣṭhyā six-day period is extended; the three-night rite is accomplished; the morning pressing is accomplished; the midday pressing is accomplished; the midday pressing is accomplished; the third pressing is accomplished; he performs ten thousand, a hundred thousand, and a million [stotras]; the midday pressing is accomplished.

The midday pressing is accomplished; the third pressing is accomplished; he proceeds with the animal offerings in their own place; the Agniṣṭoma concludes with the Dhruva cup; they produce the Ukthas; prior to them, [he offers] these two spoon-oblations.

"Juhotīndrāvaruṇayor aham," "asme indrābṛhaspatī," and "saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā"—with these [verses], they lead forward the *ukthas* for Indra and Varuṇa, for Indra and Bṛhaspati, with "saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā," for Indra and Varuṇa, for Indra and Bṛhaspati, for Indra and Viṣṇu. [M: indrā... "saṃ vāṃ karmaṇā"—for Indra... [and so on].

They introduce the *ukthas* with the words, "To Indra and Viṣṇu. The *ukthas* are successfully completed. Intending to introduce the *ṣoḍaśin*, he offers oblations with the verses "ud u tyam" and "citram," enters [the sacrificial ground], and touches the *ṣoḍaśin* cup with the verse, "From whom none other has been born... [Not in M]. Having taken hold of the golden *prastara* as sacrificial gold, he hastens with the *stotra*. He introduces the *stotra* when the sun has reached the midpoint.

He introduces the *ṣoḍaśin* stotra. Behind him, facing east, stands a horse that is reddish-brown (*aruṇapiśaṅga*). Having handed over the gold, they chant the praise. While they are chanting, he attends to them. Knowing, "This is the last [verse]," he turns away. In front of the *hotṛ*, as soon as he reaches the words "Iḍā devahūḥ" of this *yajus*, the *hotṛ* calls out to him; the *adhvaryu* responds with the word "harivat," and the *hotṛ* recites the response: "This hymn, this hymn is for Indra in speech."

Having spoken thus, he runs forward. He takes up this cup; the *camasa*-holders lift them up in succession. "Make it heard! he says. "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice to Soma! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation with the words, "Indra, sovereign lord. He offers it with: "Thou art the sovereign lord of the gods; make me a sovereign lord among men, endowed with splendor, *svāhā*! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers the oblation.

They offer the *juhoti* oblation; they offer when the *anuvaṣaṭ* has been uttered; they bring [the portions], they come back, and they consume them. Regarding that consumption, [they say]: "Indra and Samrāṭ Varuṇa the King, O Agni, first made this portion of Soma their own; may I, following their consumption, consume it—may this Soma satisfy me. Having been impelled by the *agnīdh* for the consumption of all [portions], they purify themselves with the formula, "O Brahman, move forward! The procedure for honoring [the deities] is the same. Having approached the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths...

[12.3] Having approached the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, they proceed toward the night with the verse: "O men, Indra for you from every side, Indra... He offers the oblation, and then he issues the command: "O guardian, protect the sacrifice! O *pratiprasthātṛ*, protect the speckled butter, the clarified butter, the rectum, the *viṣkalī*, and the King Soma! Let the two-cupcake for the Aśvins remain prepared and ready; let the officiating priests [be present]."

"O officiating priests, be composed; I shall lead the night; draw out the *camasa* of the *hotṛ*; O *unnetṛ*, cause the *soma* to flow forth"—with these words he addresses the *hotṛ*'s *camasa* once it has been filled, saying, "For Indra, thee! Taking the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens forward with the chant. He mutters the introductory formula, "Vāyu is the *hiṃ*-utterer," and while they are chanting, he attends upon them, saying, "May the vital breaths return to me; approach the sacrificer!"

Knowing, "This is the best," he turns away. He continues until he reaches the portion of this *yajus* formula, "The *iḍā* is the invoker of the gods for the Hotṛ. He calls out to him, and he responds. Having said, "This hymn has been recited for Indra," he runs forward; he takes up this *hotṛ-camasa*, and they lift up the *camasa*s in succession.

"O Camasādhvaryus, cause [the sacrificer] to hear!"—thus he says. "O Ukthashā, sacrifice the Soma-libations! At the *vaṣaṭ*-call they offer; at the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call they offer; they bring [the portions], they come back, and they consume [the Soma]. The formula for its consumption is: "Of that which has been offered into the fire, whose deity is Soma, which has been consecrated by Indra with the *svagā*-call, which is honey-sweet, and for which I have been invited—I, being invited, consume. Having been urged by the Agnīdh to consume the entire portion, they purify themselves. [The Adhvaryu says: "Fill the cups following the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa!"

He says, "O Adhvaryu, O Unnetṛ, come hither and prepare the Soma! He consecrates the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa which has been filled with the formula, "For Indra, thee! Having taken the *prastara* (grass-bundle), he takes this [cup] before the *iḍā*-portion of the Maitrāvaruṇa while accompanied by a hymn of praise.

They lift up this cup of Maitrāvaruṇa in succession, [saying]: "The cup has been announced to us; [O Adhvaryu], being impelled, [perform the offering]. They perform the *mārjana* purification. To the Pratiprasthātṛ, he says: "The two poles [are yours]," [and so on] for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

"Fill the goblets following the one for the *cśaṃsin*s," he says. The *pratiprasthātṛ* runs forward, saying, "O *unnetṛ*, make the Soma manifest! All the *dhura*s dedicated to Indra belong to the *pratiprasthātṛ*. In the second and third rounds, they proceed from the north of the *pratiprasthātṛ* alone; in the final round, they move as if leaping. "O *brahman*, proceed!"—this is the same [for all].
Having performed the worship at the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths... [K4 has an "EM"]. [M: ---- thus.]

[12.4] Having worshipped the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, they proceed together for the night. He offers with the verse, "O Indra, you who are on every side... O men, to Indra... Then he issues the command: "Guardian, protect the sacrifice! Pratiprasthātṛ, guard the speckled butter, the clarified butter, the rectum, the *piṣkalī*, and the King Soma! The two-cupcake for the Aśvins is cooked and ready..."

(5) "O officiating priests, be concentrated; I shall lead the night. O *hotṛ*, draw up the cup! O *unnetṛ*, prepare the Soma!"—having thus addressed them, he consecrates the drawn *hotṛ*-cup with the formula, "For Indra, thee! Taking the *prastara* grass-bundle, he hastens forward with the *astotra*. He mutters the introductory formula: "Vāyu is the *hiṅ*-singer. "Come back to me, O vital breaths; approach the sacrificer!"—with these words, he waits upon those who are chanting. Recognizing that this is the last [verse], he turns away from the front of the *hotṛ*.
Reciting "iḍā devahūḥ," as far as this *yajus* extends, he calls out to him; he responds to him. Having said, "This hymn (*uktha*), this hymn is for Indra in speech," he runs forward.

He takes this *hotṛ*’s cup while the other cups are being lifted after it; he says, "Proclaim!"—"O reciter of the *uktha*, [proclaim] the Soma! At the *vaṣaṭ*-call they offer, at the secondary *vaṣaṭ*-call they offer; they bring [the cups], they come back, and they consume. Its formula for consumption is: "Of the Soma offered into the fire, whose deity is Soma, which has been consecrated by Indra with the *svagā*-call, which is honeyed, and for which I have been invited—I, being invited, consume. Having been urged by the *agnīdh* to consume the entire portion, they purify themselves. "Fill the *maitrāvaruṇa*’s cup after [the *hotṛ*’s]," [he says].

Thus the Adhvaryu says as they run forward: "O Unnetṛ, let them cause the Soma to flow forth. He should consecrate the Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup with the formula, "For Indra thee! Having taken the *prastara* (grass-bundle), he [performs] with the chant—previously [for the Maitrāvaruṇa’s *iḍā* etc.]—he takes this Maitrāvaruṇa’s cup; they lift up the cups in succession; he causes [the announcement] to be heard; when [the sacrifice] is impelled, they purify themselves. The Pratiprasthātṛ says, "The two poles are ready," and he says, "Fill the cups following the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin’s cup. They run forward; the Pratiprasthātṛ says to the Unnetṛ: "O Unnetṛ..."

"Exalt the Soma"—thus [the Pratiprasthātṛ] performs all the duties pertaining to Indra on the north side; thus the second round, thus the third; with this final round they proceed as if winding around. "O Brahman, move forward"—thus, having likewise approached the four hearths (dhiṣṇiya).
Thus:

Having paid homage to the four *dhiṣṇiya* hearths, they proceed together for the *saṃdhya* chant of the *rathantara*. Then he issues the command: "Fill the cups following the cup of the *hotṛ*; O *unnetṛ*, make the *soma* swell. He consecrates the cup of the *hotṛ* once it has been filled with: "Thee for the Aśvins! Having touched the cup of the *hotṛ* which contains the sacrificial cake and having taken the *prastara* bundle, he stands to the east of the *hotṛ* and responds to him at the *iḍā* offering.

The Hotṛ recites the *āśvina* hymn for a thousand verses; having said, "This is the hymn (*uktha*), it is spoken for Indra," he hastens forward, saying, "Recite the invitatory verse for the *soma*s drawn on the previous day for the Aśvins! Take this *puroḍāśa* cake! The *camasa* cups are lifted up following the *hotṛcamasa*; he says, "O, cause [the *śrauṣaṭ*] to be heard!"—"Recite the offering verse for the *soma* of the one who has recited the hymn (*ukthaśas*)."
When the *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered, he offers the sacrificial cake; when the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* has been uttered,
they offer, they bring [the portions], they come back, and they consume [them].

Its portion is that which has been offered in the fire, dedicated to the deity Soma, known by the *ativid*, consecrated with *svagā* for the Aśvins, and mixed with honey; the Āgnīdhra gives the impulse, and they perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*) with the formula, "O Prajāpati, he knows.
Then, intending to lead the *aptoryāma*, he offers with, "O Prajāpati, he knows. Thereafter, he issues the command: "Fill the cups following the Hotṛ’s cup; O Unnetṛ, make the Soma flow forth.
He consecrates the Hotṛ’s cup once it has been filled with, "For Agni, thee."
Having taken the sacrificial grass-bundle (prastara), he hastens with the chant;
at each stotra he performs the introductory rite (upākaraṇa); when the chanting is finished, they bring [the Soma], they come back, and they consume it.
"O Soma-deities, this is the food for him that has been offered into the fire and consecrated by *svagā* with fire; [the priests] purify themselves with honey.

[The Adhvaryu] says, "Fill the *camasa* of the Maitrāvaruṇa after [your own]; come quickly, O Adhvaryus, do not let the Soma go to waste! Having taken the *prastara* [grass-bundle], he recites over the filled *camasa* of the Maitrāvaruṇa, "For Indra thee!", and runs toward the *stotra*.
While they are praising, they bring [the portions], they come, and they consume them.

The formula for consuming that is: "Of the Soma offered into the fire, having Soma as its deity, consecrated by Indra with the *svagā* call, [the portion] of honey... Having purified themselves, the Adhvaryu says, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, these two yokes are yours. Running forward, the Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ proceed with both [formulas], namely, with the one addressed to the Viśve Devas and the one addressed to Viṣṇu.
Then he gives the command: "O Brahman, proceed! Having uttered the *nisarpana*-yajus formula, he again gives the command: "O Āgnīdhra, bring the embers for the *upayaja* offerings!
With eight portions of the rectum, the *upayaṣṭṛ* performs the *upayaja* offerings.
The Āptoryāma sacrifice is concluded with the well-known Agniṣṭoma rite.
[End of section] Thus ends the *Pavitra* consisting of ten oblations.

Then he pours out the *pavitra* offering consisting of ten oblations: "To Agni Pavamāna, a cake on eight potsherds; to Agni Pāvaka, a cake on eight potsherds; to Agni Śuci, a cake on eight potsherds; to Agni Vratapati, a cake on eight potsherds; and to Vaiśvānara, a cake on twelve potsherds.
While taking the portions of clarified butter, he takes them into the *dhruvā* vessel; having cooked them, he sets them down.
There are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses.

Having recited the *sāmidhenīs*, he invokes the deities: "O Agni, bring Agni; bring Soma"—thus for the two *ājyabhāga* portions—"bring Agni Pavamāna; bring Sarasvatī the beloved; bring Agni Pāvaka; bring Vāyu with his team (*niyutvant*); bring Agni; bring Agni Śuci; bring the god Savitṛ; bring Agni Vratapati; bring Dadhikrāvan; bring Vaiśvānara; bring Viṣṇu. Thus he says.

Having performed the *prayāja* offerings and stepped across without delay, he bastes the *dhruvā* ladle; then the cake, then the *dhruvā*, then the cake, then the *dhruvā*, then the cake, then the *dhruvā*, then the cake, and finally the *upabhṛt* ladle.
He offers the two *ājyabhāga* portions, reciting the two *vārtraghna* verses for the *ājyabhāgas*.
While cutting off portions of the cake, he says: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Pavamāna!"
Having recited, "O Agni, you purify our lives," he offers the oblation with, "O Agni, purify yourself.
While taking the clarified butter, he says, "Recite for Sarasvatī, the beloved.
Having recited, "By Truth, for the beloved ones," he offers the oblation with, "These [oblations], being offered, bestowing long life upon us with reverences."
While about to eat of the *puroḍāśa* cake itself, he says, "Recite for Agni Pāvaka";

having recited, "O Agni Pāvaka, with thy radiance," he offers the oblation with, "O purifying one, shining for us. While taking portions of the clarified butter (*ājya*) itself, he says, "Recite for Vāyu Niyutvat."
Having recited "O Vāyu, [come] with a hundred bay horses," he offers the oblation with the verse, "With thy steeds thou goest to the donor.
While cutting portions from the sacrificial cake itself, he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni Śuci.
Having recited, "Agni, most observant of pure vows," he offers the oblation with the verse, "Upward, O Agni, rise thy pure [flames]."
While taking portions of the clarified butter itself, he says, "Recite for Savitṛ, O gods!

Having recited, "O divine Savitṛ, today [favor us]," he offers the sacrifice with, "O divine Savitṛ, [grant] all [things]. While cutting portions from the sacrificial cake itself, he says, "Recite for Agni Vratapati."
Having recited, "O Agni, you are the guardian of vows," he offers with, "Whatever of your vows we have violated.
Taking a portion of clarified butter, he says, "Recite for Dadhikrāvin.
Having recited, "I have performed [the praise] for Dadhikrāvan," he offers with, "O Dadhikrā."
While cutting portions from the *puroḍāśa* itself, he says, "Recite for Vaiśvānara! He recites [the verse]:
"For Vaiśvānara of broad majesty... the inspired poets bestow jewels upon the foundations so that he may go; for Agni, the immortal, honors the gods, and thus he has established those laws together."

He sacrifices with the verse, "O Agni, you... [RV 6.48.1]: "Flaming, at birth, you filled the two worlds; may the gods delight in you who are beyond reproach. Having recited the verses for Jātavedas, beginning with "O Vaiśvānara, by your greatness...
and taking the *ājya* with "For Viṣṇu...," and having recited "Viṣṇu strode across this [world]," he sacrifices with the verse, "May I attain that beloved domain of his."

The two *saṃyājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* metre if he sacrifices with the *iṣṭi*; they are in the *anuṣṭubh* metre if he is about to sacrifice with Soma. This very *pavitra* [purification] purifies the ten oblations as the limbs by means of the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*), and the vital breaths (*prāṇa*) by means of the clarified butter (*ājya*). Just as, for example, here on earth, people do not accept a child [in their lap] if he is in the middle of a pit... (26)... [they do not accept him].

Peṃkhaśa . . . (4) Pāpman indeed becomes manifest to Satyadeva. . . . They do not accept him as pure or fit for sacrifice; they do not eat his oblation. But he who, having sacrificed with this [offering], sacrifices with Soma—the gods accept him as pure and fit for sacrifice, and they eat his oblation. Moreover, if one should think that he has acted as if mixed [with impurity], then he should sacrifice with this [offering].

He should think thus, or he should sacrifice: "To Vaiśvānara, the conqueror of the *kṣatra*, [he offers] a cake on twelve potsherds; he takes [the portion] from the earth... he places it upon the [hearth] after it has been cooked. With three [verses... he sets it down.

(21) He deposits three [bricks]. There are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings are the *vārtraghna* hymns, for "they did not find any other spy besides him, for whose ancient paths these were in the beginning" (*yeṣām ime pūrve armāsa āsan*). The two *triṣṭubh* verses are the *saṃyājyā*s for the oblation. It concludes in the established manner. Having sacrificed with this [offering], Satyaśravasa [attained his goal].
Hariḥ Śrīrāma Namaḥ Hariḥ. Thus ends [the section].
